### Users see "Need admin approval" when they connect

When users connect to Microsoft SharePoint from the Gemini Enterprise web
app for the first time, Microsoft might show a Need admin approval
screen. This happens if Gemini Enterprise requests administrator-level
permissions, or if your Microsoft Entra tenant prohibits users from authorizing
third-party apps without prior tenant-wide administrator consent.

To resolve this issue, an administrator must complete the first authorization.
After that, other users in your tenant can connect without the approval screen.

-
Ask a Microsoft Entra ID administrator who can grant tenant-wide consent to
sign in to the Gemini Enterprise web app and connect to
Microsoft SharePoint.

-
On the permissions screen, have the administrator select Consent on behalf
of your organization, and then click Accept.

-
Ask users to connect again.

For more information, see
Grant tenant-wide admin consent
in the Microsoft Entra documentation.

Note: Deleting and re-creating the data store doesn't resolve this issue,
because consent is granted in your Microsoft Entra tenant, not to the data store.

## Set up authentication and permissions

You need to set up authentication and permissions in Microsoft Entra admin center. This is crucial for allowing the connector to access and synchronize data.

-
Grant administrator consent. For information about how to grant consent, see
Grant tenant-wide administrator consent to an
application in the Microsoft Entra documentation.

Caution:

- Tenant-wide administrator consent (CRITICAL): You must grant tenant-wide administrator consent in Microsoft Entra ID for the registered application. Lack of administrator consent is a common failure point that prevents the connector from authenticating.

- Dual App IDs: Note that Gemini Enterprise uses different Microsoft Entra App IDs for different features. You need one App ID for the backend 'Data store' connection and a separate App ID to enable the 'Upload from OneDrive/SharePoint' button in the chat interface. Both applications require administrator consent.

## Troubleshooting

This section describes how to resolve common issues with the Microsoft SharePoint
connector.

## Filter types

You can configure the following filters within the `params` object of your data connector:

- Inclusion filter (`admin_filter`): Retrieves only specific information from the
Microsoft SharePoint data store.

- Exclusion filter (`admin_exclusion_filter`): Excludes specific information from the Microsoft SharePoint
data store.

- Legacy filter (`structured_search_filter`): Previously used to create a data store with filters using the API.

## Limitations

This section outlines known issues and limitations that may affect your use of the Microsoft SharePoint data store.

- When creating a new app or adding a data store to an existing one, it's recommended to associate only one data store with actions belonging to a single connector type.

- Enforcing a VPC Service Controls perimeter on existing Microsoft SharePoint data stores is not supported.
To enforce VPC Service Controls, you must delete and recreate the data stores. For more information on VPC Service Controls
and how to use actions after enabling VPC Service Controls, see Secure your app with VPC Service Controls.

- The Microsoft SharePoint data store is supported only in the
`global`, `us`, and `eu`
locations.

- Search quality prerequisite: To achieve optimal search results and fully leverage Knowledge Graph features, we recommend configuring and syncing the People search data store in addition to the Microsoft SharePoint data store.

The following are the limitations for the Microsoft SharePoint federated data store:

- Default write actions: When creating and configuring the data store, ensure that any default write actions are explicitly disabled if you only intend to grant read access. Leaving write actions enabled without the corresponding write scopes in Microsoft Entra ID results in authentication and sync errors.

-

If the create data store flow shows an Advanced options section, you can select the Enable Static IP Addresses checkbox within it. This ensures the data store uses a fixed set of IP addresses for outbound traffic, suitable for allowlisting on the source system. For more information, see Configure static IP egress.

-

In the Configuration section:

- From the Multi-region list, select the location for your data connector.

- In the Your data connector name field, enter a name for your connector.

- If you selected `us` or `eu` as the location,
configure the Encryption settings:

- Optional: If you haven't configured single-region keys, click Go to settings page to do so. For more information, see Register a single-region key for third-party connectors.

- Select Google-managed encryption key or Cloud KMS key.

- If you selected Cloud KMS key:

- If you selected Data ingestion, continue with the following steps:

- Optional: To sync specific projects, do the following:

- Click Filter.

- To filter entities out of the index, select the Exclude from the index checkbox, or to ensure that they are included in the index, select the Include to the index checkbox.

- Enter the keys. Press enter after each key.

- Click Save.

- To configure the sync schedule, do the following:

- In the Sync frequency list, select the sync frequency.

- To schedule separate full syncs of entity and identity data, expand the menu in the Full sync section and then select Custom options.

- In the Incremental sync frequency list, select the incremental sync frequency.
For more information, see Sync schedules.

-
Click Continue.

-
In the Actions section:

- If you selected Federated search:

- From Select Microsoft SharePoint actions to enable, select the actions from the category to enable them for the connector.

-
If you selected Data ingestion:

-
In the Authentication settings section, configure authentication based on your chosen connection mode.

-
Provide the following authentication details as necessary:

-
On the data store Data page, wait until the Connector state changes
to Active.

-
In the Real-time sync field, click View/edit.

-
To enable real-time sync, click the Enable real-time sync toggle.

-
In the Client secret field, enter a value. This value is used to verify
Microsoft SharePoint webhook events. We recommend using a string of 20 characters.

-
Click Save.

Wait for the Real-time sync field to change to Running.

## Supported actions

When the Microsoft SharePoint data store is enabled, end users can use natural language commands in Gemini Enterprise to perform the following actions.

| Action
| Description

| Create folder
| Creates a new folder in a specified path.

| Add list
| Creates a new structured data list (for example, tasks, contacts) on the Microsoft SharePoint site.

| Upload document
| Uploads a document to a Microsoft SharePoint site or library.

| Download document
| Downloads a document from a Microsoft SharePoint site or library.

| Add page
| Creates a new page on the Microsoft SharePoint site.

| Check out document
| Check out a document from a Microsoft SharePoint library.

| Check in document
| Check a document into a Microsoft SharePoint library.

| Rename attachment or document
| Rename an attachment or document in a Microsoft SharePoint library.

| Move attachment or document
| Move a document from a Microsoft SharePoint library to a destination
library, folder, or another SharePoint site.

| Discard check out document
| Discards a check-out on a document, reverting it without saving changes.

### Impact of a subject value change

If the value that's mapped to `google.subject` changes for a user, then
Gemini Enterprise treats the user as a new user. For example, this happens
when the user's user principal name (UPN) or email address changes in Microsoft
Entra ID and your attribute mapping uses that attribute. Principal identifiers
are case-sensitive, so a change in letter case is also a change.

After the change, the following applies:

- The user can't access the chat history, notebooks, or agents that are
associated with the previous principal identifier.

- Gemini Enterprise doesn't migrate data from the previous principal
identifier to the new principal identifier.

- Licenses and IAM roles that are granted to the previous
principal identifier don't apply to the new principal identifier.

## Troubleshoot authentication errors

If users get HTTP `401` errors that report invalid authentication credentials
when they access Gemini Enterprise, check the following.

### Prepare for a subject value change

To reduce the impact of a subject value change, do the following:

- Before you change a user's UPN or email address in your identity provider,
inform the user and ask them to
share any private agents or notebooks that
they want to keep.

- Assign a Gemini Enterprise license to the new principal identifier, and
grant the required roles to it. For more information, see
Grant permissions to users.

- Transfer ownership of the agents
that the user shared with others to the new principal identifier. You can't
transfer ownership of agents that aren't shared.

## User identity changes

Gemini Enterprise associates a user's chat history, notebooks, and the
agents that the user creates with the user's principal identifier. If you use
Workforce Identity Federation, the principal identifier includes the value that your
attribute mapping assigns to `google.subject`. For example:

`principal://iam.googleapis.com/locations/global/workforcePools/POOL_ID/subject/SUBJECT_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE`

## Troubleshoot 401 and 403 sign-in errors

The following table lists common `401` and `403` sign-in errors and how to
resolve them:

| Error
| Resolution

|
`401: Request had invalid authentication credentials`

|
Synchronize your device clock with an NTP server (even a 1-minute clock
skew invalidates authentication tokens), clear your browser cookies, and
retry in an incognito window.

|
`403: Forbidden / Permission Denied`

|
Verify the following in order:

-
The user, federated `principal://`, or
`principalSet://` identifier (not
`user:EMAIL`) has the
`roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceUser` or
`roles/discoveryengine.user` role and an active license.

-
Third-party IdP group claims are within token limits. For example,
Microsoft Entra ID limits claims to 150 groups for SAML or 200
groups for OIDC. For more information, see Configure
Workforce Identity Federation with Microsoft Entra ID and a large
number of groups and Configure
attribute mapping.

-
Gemini Enterprise is turned on for the user's organizational unit in
the Google Workspace Admin console.

|
`403: WidgetService.LookupWidgetConfig`
(`The caller does not have permission`)

## Troubleshooting SharePoint connector search results

If you are experiencing issues with missing documents, incorrect results, or poor search relevance, check the following diagnostic areas:

- Check the People data store: Ensure the People search data store is set up and syncing if you face relevance or entity-matching issues.

- Authentication errors: Persistent authentication errors, such as "Error when retrieving Graph API access token," will prevent searches from functioning. To resolve this, check the Microsoft Entra ID logs for details and then re-authenticate the connection.

- Identity mismatch (data ingestion mode): When using data ingestion mode
with Google Identity, verify that each user's Google email address matches
their Microsoft email address. Mismatches prevent Gemini Enterprise
from returning search results.

- Targeted folder searches (.aspx URLs): Searching with full browser URLs that end in `/Forms/AllItems.aspx` executes a search across the whole site, not just the specific folder. Always use absolute folder paths for targeted searches.

- Result limits: Be aware that federated searches may have limits on the number of documents returned per query (typically capping around 20 results).

- Citation issues: Intermittent incorrect citations can occur. If persistent, report the issue to support and include your diagnostic tokens.

- Connector-model compatibility: Ensure you are using the latest Gemini model versions. Some older models (for example, 3.x) have known issues resolving tools for SharePoint actions, such as `download_document` within Agent Builder.

app for the first time, Microsoft might show a Need admin approval
screen. This happens if Gemini Enterprise requests administrator-level
permissions, or if your Microsoft Entra tenant prohibits users from authorizing
third-party apps without prior tenant-wide administrator consent.

To resolve this issue, an administrator must complete the first authorization.
After that, other users in your tenant can connect without the approval screen.

Ask a Microsoft Entra ID administrator who can grant tenant-wide consent to
sign in to the Gemini Enterprise web app and connect to
Microsoft SharePoint.

On the permissions screen, have the administrator select Consent on behalf

Ask users to connect again.

For more information, see

in the Microsoft Entra documentation.

because consent is granted in your Microsoft Entra tenant, not to the data store.

Grant administrator consent. For information about how to grant consent, see
Grant tenant-wide administrator consent to an
application in the Microsoft Entra documentation.

## Troubleshooting SharePoint connector search results

If you are experiencing issues with missing documents, incorrect results, or poor search relevance, check the following diagnostic areas:

- Check the People data store: Ensure the People search data store is set up and syncing if you face relevance or entity-matching issues.

- Authentication errors: Persistent authentication errors, such as "Error when retrieving Graph API access token," will prevent searches from functioning. To resolve this, check the Microsoft Entra ID logs for details and then re-authenticate the connection.

- Identity mismatch (data ingestion mode): When using data ingestion mode
with Google Identity, verify that each user's Google email address matches
their Microsoft email address. Mismatches prevent Gemini Enterprise
from returning search results.

- Targeted folder searches (.aspx URLs): Searching with full browser URLs that end in `/Forms/AllItems.aspx` executes a search across the whole site, not just the specific folder. Always use absolute folder paths for targeted searches.

The Microsoft SharePoint data store for Gemini Enterprise lets you search and perform actions on your Microsoft SharePoint Online data, including documents, lists, and sites.

Note: When using federated search or federated connectors, your query string is sent to all enabled third-party search backends. The query string sent to a third-party system might contain parts of the data in your search request and conversation history. The third-party system can link the query with your identity. Once data is in the third-party system, it is subject to that system's Terms of Service and privacy policies, not Google Cloud's Terms of Service.

### Query execution

After you authorize Microsoft SharePoint and send a search query to Gemini Enterprise:

- Gemini Enterprise sends your search query directly to the Microsoft API.

- Gemini Enterprise blends the results with those from other connected data sources and displays a comprehensive search result.
To successfully connect Gemini Enterprise with Microsoft SharePoint, you must complete the following configuration steps.

- Result limits: Be aware that federated searches may have limits on the number of documents returned per query (typically capping around 20 results).

- Citation issues: Intermittent incorrect citations can occur. If persistent, report the issue to support and include your diagnostic tokens.

- Connector-model compatibility: Ensure you are using the latest Gemini model versions. Some older models (for example, 3.x) have known issues resolving tools for SharePoint actions, such as `download_document` within Agent Builder.

### Impact of a subject value change

If the value that's mapped to `google.subject` changes for a user, then
Gemini Enterprise treats the user as a new user. For example, this happens
when the user's user principal name (UPN) or email address changes in Microsoft
Entra ID and your attribute mapping uses that attribute. Principal identifiers
are case-sensitive, so a change in letter case is also a change.

After the change, the following applies:

- The user can't access the chat history, notebooks, or agents that are
associated with the previous principal identifier.

- Gemini Enterprise doesn't migrate data from the previous principal
identifier to the new principal identifier.

- Licenses and IAM roles that are granted to the previous
principal identifier don't apply to the new principal identifier.

### Prepare for a subject value change

To reduce the impact of a subject value change, do the following:

- Before you change a user's UPN or email address in your identity provider,
inform the user and ask them to
share any private agents or notebooks that
they want to keep.

- Assign a Gemini Enterprise license to the new principal identifier, and
grant the required roles to it. For more information, see
Grant permissions to users.

- Transfer ownership of the agents
that the user shared with others to the new principal identifier. You can't
transfer ownership of agents that aren't shared.

### Users see "Need admin approval" when they connect

When users connect to Microsoft SharePoint from the Gemini Enterprise web
app for the first time, Microsoft might show a Need admin approval
screen. This happens if Gemini Enterprise requests administrator-level
permissions, or if your Microsoft Entra tenant prohibits users from authorizing
third-party apps without prior tenant-wide administrator consent.

To resolve this issue, an administrator must complete the first authorization.
After that, other users in your tenant can connect without the approval screen.

-
Ask a Microsoft Entra ID administrator who can grant tenant-wide consent to
sign in to the Gemini Enterprise web app and connect to
Microsoft SharePoint.

-
On the permissions screen, have the administrator select Consent on behalf
of your organization, and then click Accept.

-
Ask users to connect again.

For more information, see
Grant tenant-wide admin consent
in the Microsoft Entra documentation.

Note: Deleting and re-creating the data store doesn't resolve this issue,
because consent is granted in your Microsoft Entra tenant, not to the data store.

## Set up authentication and permissions

You need to set up authentication and permissions in Microsoft Entra admin center. This is crucial for allowing the connector to access and synchronize data.

-
Grant administrator consent. For information about how to grant consent, see
Grant tenant-wide administrator consent to an
application in the Microsoft Entra documentation.

Caution:

- Tenant-wide administrator consent (CRITICAL): You must grant tenant-wide administrator consent in Microsoft Entra ID for the registered application. Lack of administrator consent is a common failure point that prevents the connector from authenticating.

- Dual App IDs: Note that Gemini Enterprise uses different Microsoft Entra App IDs for different features. You need one App ID for the backend 'Data store' connection and a separate App ID to enable the 'Upload from OneDrive/SharePoint' button in the chat interface. Both applications require administrator consent.

## Filter types

You can configure the following filters within the `params` object of your data connector:

- Inclusion filter (`admin_filter`): Retrieves only specific information from the
Microsoft SharePoint data store.

- Exclusion filter (`admin_exclusion_filter`): Excludes specific information from the Microsoft SharePoint
data store.

- Legacy filter (`structured_search_filter`): Previously used to create a data store with filters using the API.

## Troubleshooting SharePoint connector search results

If you are experiencing issues with missing documents, incorrect results, or poor search relevance, check the following diagnostic areas:

- Check the People data store: Ensure the People search data store is set up and syncing if you face relevance or entity-matching issues.

- Authentication errors: Persistent authentication errors, such as "Error when retrieving Graph API access token," will prevent searches from functioning. To resolve this, check the Microsoft Entra ID logs for details and then re-authenticate the connection.

- Identity mismatch (data ingestion mode): When using data ingestion mode
with Google Identity, verify that each user's Google email address matches
their Microsoft email address. Mismatches prevent Gemini Enterprise
from returning search results.

- Targeted folder searches (.aspx URLs): Searching with full browser URLs that end in `/Forms/AllItems.aspx` executes a search across the whole site, not just the specific folder. Always use absolute folder paths for targeted searches.

### Query execution

After you authorize Microsoft SharePoint and send a search query to Gemini Enterprise:

- Gemini Enterprise sends your search query directly to the Microsoft API.

- Gemini Enterprise blends the results with those from other connected data sources and displays a comprehensive search result.

To successfully connect Gemini Enterprise with Microsoft SharePoint, you must complete the following configuration steps.

- Result limits: Be aware that federated searches may have limits on the number of documents returned per query (typically capping around 20 results).

- Citation issues: Intermittent incorrect citations can occur. If persistent, report the issue to support and include your diagnostic tokens.

- Connector-model compatibility: Ensure you are using the latest Gemini model versions. Some older models (for example, 3.x) have known issues resolving tools for SharePoint actions, such as `download_document` within Agent Builder.
